newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices talked higher on oil rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices talked higher on oil rally.

text.p: Spot values in the U.S. residual fuel oil market were talked higher on an oil rally sparked by news that United Nations suspended the Iraqi oil-for-aid deal.

Although suppliers were eager for the opportunity to sell at higher prices, end-users were equally content to stay on the sideline because of attractive natural gas prices and low electricity demand, industry sources said.
Higher prices assessments in the U.S. were downplayed by the absence of any reported physical transactions today, traders said.
NYMEX October crude futures settled up $1.15 at $23.40 a barrel after posting a four-month high of $24.25 on news on U.S.-led attacks on Iraqi military sites over the weekend.
Offers increased up to 50 cents per barrel across the board, but bids were mostly unchanged, traders said, adding fuel oil prices in Europe rose six dollars per tonne.
"We haven't have the same follow through in the U.S.," said one Houston trader, referring to the lack of trades.
New York Harbor prompt one percent were assessed at $16.75-$17.25 a barrel, compared with Friday's $16.50-$17.00. High sulphurs in NYH were little changed.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent was discussed at $15.75-$16.25, a wider range than Friday's $15.75-$16.00, traders said.
USG three percent was pegged at $14.50-$15.00, compared with $14.50-$15.00 on Friday, traders said.
New York city gate September gas prices rose to $2.06/ mmBtu level, versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.69/mmBtu equivalent.
